assessments.topic: Actual identity and RO mapping before import
assessments.result: SETUP uses the actual owned Root/child, retains the actual Cocoa window, obtains the ordinary v2 Root epoch/identity and lease, queries actual self birth/session, opens the producer reader, and creates a real exported CAContext. PREPARE captures the known ticket and opens the corresponding host reader with the full identity. INSTALL requires a readable snapshot from that reader and uses only the known ticket. Basis status_cell.c:84-94 opens READ|QUERY and maps PAGE_READONLY; no fixture writer or synthetic SAFE path is introduced.

The observer runs synchronously through OnMainThread against the retained actual Root window. It independently counts actual parent sublayers by globally allocated ticket, exact context/ticket ledger entries, and current C selections. It performs no removal, completion, status publication, or NT control. Missing parent/view and exceptions do not produce a valid zero witness. CHECK13 requires attached=ledger=indexed=1; CHECK16 requires a valid actual zero witness plus HostSAFE; CHECK17 requires the same context still owned and epoch/lease/ticket unchanged.

PREPARE, INSTALL, CANCEL, and RELEASE attempts are latched before dispatch. Unknown delivery returns pending rather than operation success; INSTALL is never automatically replayed. The normal client requires successful SETUP/PREPARE/INSTALL and bounded correlated frames; CANCEL and RELEASE pending replies are followed by actual SAFE reads. Failure after an attempted install preserves the exported context until actual host-or-producer SAFE evidence and actual Cocoa absence. A late/failed call cannot qualify a 25/0 pass merely through subsequent cleanup.

The normal path observes HostSAFE and actual model absence while retaining the context, explicitly releases the producer, then observes ProducerSAFE before cleanup. Cleanup latches resource_safe only after a real SAFE read plus valid absence, and producer_safe only from an actual SAFE_ONLY read with invalid dynamic values. These latches are set before reader close can invalidate a view. A subsequent local-close retry therefore need not recover SAFE from a closing reader. The actual status-cell close retains remaining view/handle ownership on NT error; cleanup reports that error and retains the window/module/root rather than treating local close as completed.

Context-release attempt is recorded before the actual void destroy call, and ownership is cleared only after it returns; an indeterminate repeated destroy is rejected. Successful cleanup requires the context, both local NT readers, and retained Cocoa window all gone. The normal client then destroys its actual child/Root, unloads the driver, and unregisters the class. Ordinary failure cleanup runs the helper first and preserves those client owners when helper cleanup remains unresolved.

QPC frequency and monotonicity are checked with multiplication overflow bounded. Each helper operation has a four-second elapsed rejection after JSON emission/flush. Each poll shares a four-second start, so individual iterations do not renew the budget. Nonzero helper/NT status, malformed/crossed frames, late returns, incomplete check counts, cleanup failure, and output errors prevent success. Deadlines reject late completion after return; they do not preempt a blocked foreign call.

The fixed-width frame is 128 bytes with asserted epoch offset32 and read-result offset72; it contains no cross-bitness pointers. The stdcall export matches the client WINAPI pointer. The private PE SRW lock serializes controls; no held task or callback fixture reentry is introduced by these fragments. Actual enum/table/Unix-call integration and paired binaries remain parent binding work.

report.admission_scope: Source admission of the supplied ordinary, same-process, known-ticket graphics lifecycle fixture with current v2 client. No concrete P1/P2 found in this bounded scope. Runtime qualification and integrated dependency binding are separate.
limits: No build, test, candidate execution, network, source edit, runtime control, or inspection/resumption of the separate blocked NT-failure/concurrency fixture. Only this requested report was written.
Parent build reports are not verification. No actual 25/0 result, cleanup receipt, paired PE/Native binding, or runtime admission is asserted.

The four-second checks are elapsed rejection guards. The external controller must enforce an outer watchdog for blocking NT, USER, Cocoa, destruction, module/window/class cleanup, or output calls; those calls are not forcibly preempted by this client.

Cleanup summary describes the helper/local owned resources and client cleanup attempts. In particular, an unknown ACQUIRE before a lease/producer reader is captured cannot prove server quiescence through this helper; that run already fails SETUP, and Root revocation plus independent external cleanup evidence is required. Do not use cleanup=true alone as a whole-server drain receipt.

The normal path retains context through ProducerSAFE. Failure cleanup may release a never-imported context immediately, or an attempted-import context after actual HostSAFE plus model absence while still waiting for ProducerSAFE; it does not claim producer quiescence from that earlier context release.

The observer counts actual model/layer ownership only. No GPU retirement, presented pixel, rendering correctness, cross-process, performance, real NT-failure, protection, negative, or race acceptance claim is supported.

Full underlying page wire semantics, ordinary server lifecycle, and protocol/message admission were previously reviewed and were not globally re-audited. Basis reads were restricted to the fixture-used sender, prepare/install/cancel, exported-context, and status-reader ownership mechanics.
